analysis:
The changed files are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (about 38 added lines near head 451-488, outside the supplied head text units, plus later sections that appear unchanged) and docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md (patch hunks at head 158, 182-219, 285-288, 300-304). No code, protocol, key, attestation, or storage behavior changes in this diff, so no control is demonstrably weakened.

The docs describe new selected-model recovery behavior in ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift and ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift. Recovery retries operator-selected models that memory kept out. It may evict resident models, including adopted Autopilot slots with no unexpired hold, only within an operation's victim rules and excluding the ordinary selection, pins, and advertised models a request could reload. It releases an adoption ten minutes after the later of the hold's expiry and the moment the selected model began waiting. It pauses on an add-on hold (TB-012/T-059) and cancels an attempt in progress.

Security-relevant questions for later passes, none provable from this docs-only diff:
- The implementation is not supplied, so the described invariants cannot be verified. These are the hold, lease, and pin protections, and the claim that recovery never evicts a held slot.
- The new release path touches availability (A-018) and adoption semantics (T-059, T-060).
- Eviction of adopted models must not bypass the weight-hash and self-test gates, and a model reload must not occur during an add-on hold.
- The line 'policy pending owner review' in the doc indicates the release policy is not finalized.
- Whether the enabled_models restart-needed behavior leaves stale advertisement is also unverified.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected. The hardware-support sections in the supplied units describe memory admission and cluster batching, make no new qualification claims, and assert no changes to trust boundaries.
